title: Prioritized export onramp and self-serve contracts for enterprise telemetry
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Enterprise customers submit diverse console/reporting requests (ad-hoc exports, cost breakdowns, tenant-level dashboards). Current intake is noisy, lacks deterministic prioritization, and creates erratic engineering SLAs. Goal: create a prioritized 'onramp' for telemetry exports and analytics requests that (1) surfaces a deterministic eligibility check and cost estimate, (2) routes requests to self-serve vs concierge lanes, and (3) produces a contract + SLA template for delivered exports. Scope: intake form design, server-side scoring function, routing rules, self-serve export contract template, engineering acceptance criteria, and a lightweight reporting audit trail in the Console. Out of scope: building full BI connectors (we will hand off to connector roadmap).
acceptance_criteria: New intake form added to Console which collects dataset sample, destination type, desired cadence, privacy constraints, and business justification
Automated scoring returns eligibility (eligible | review | denied) with cost estimate and suggested lane
Self-serve lane supports CSV and S3 snapshot exports with tenant-aware rate limits and retention config
Concierge lane converts eligible-but-complex requests into a templated delivery contract (SLA, retention, cost), visible to customer success
Audit log entry is created for each accepted export with links to execution job and owner
Security review completed for export flows that include PII or cross-tenant aggregation
decisions: Use server-side scoring instead of manual triage to reduce time-to-first-response; initial model will be rule-based (weighting for dataset size, frequency, PII flag)
Treat streaming/real-time exports as concierge-only for first 3 months to limit infra risk
Expose cost-estimate bands (Low/Medium/High) rather than per-token line item in MVP to avoid quoting precision issues
Integrate S3/BigQuery destinations as prioritized targets; leave direct BI connector work to separate epics
notes: Tradeoffs: automated scoring reduces manual overhead but may under-classify nuanced privacy needs; we will add 'requester notes' field and escalation path
We recommend a 2-week pilot with 3 enterprise customers (Alpha customers identified by AMs) before broader rollout
Design will provide an embedded cost estimator UI (mockups in drive link) and small copy changes to set expectations
Engineering: initial delivery requires small ingestion + jobs API, plus a short-lived export runner; ops will add quotas per tenant
dependencies: PM-110001 (Auth: tenant RBAC enforcement for exports)
SEC-4321 (Privacy review pipeline and PII detection hook)
timeline_summary: Week 1-2: finalize intake schema, design mockups, and rule-based scoring weights
Week 3-4: engineering builds intake endpoint, scoring service, and basic CSV/S3 snapshot runner
Week 5: pilot with 3 enterprise customers, collect feedback and failure modes
Week 6: resolve pilot feedback, finalize contract template, security signoff, and GA rollout
acceptance_rubric_examples: Example: Tenant A requests daily S3 snapshots of usage by workspace. Score: eligible - low cost. Routed to self-serve with 24-hr SLA for first run and 7-day retention default
Example: Tenant B requests hourly streaming cost metrics containing customer PII. Score: review - flagged for SEC and concierge lane with contract that includes encryption and audit requirements
risk_mitigation: Limit initial export concurrency per tenant to 2 jobs to prevent noisy neighbors
Add circuit-breaker on export runner that pauses exports if error rate > 5% for 10m
Add mandatory CS/AM notification for any export that requests full-tenant aggregates or PII fields
follow_up_tasks: Create templated delivery contract and SLA doc for concierge deliveries
Instrument telemetry for intake funnel conversion and avg TTR (time to respond)
Add a feedback loop: allow customers to rate exports (satisfaction + accuracy) for 90 days after delivery
